Arb-certified leading-minor signs of the even and odd carrier Gram matrices for K = 2..9 at 14 apertures omega in [1/1000, 1/2] (224 cells, 512-bit balls, none unresolved) match (-1)^{r(r-1)/2} and (-1)^{r(r+1)/2}; Jacobi counts equal the proved inertia; mpmath eigenvalue inertia agrees for K = 2..7 at omega = 1/20, 1/5, 1/3, 1/2; carrier Gram entries equal the Andreief convolution integrals to 1e-40
beyond the half aperture certified minor signs break the pattern (e.g. K = 3 at omega = 4/5 and 9/10), and at a = 3 pi/2 a pair factor is positive: the hypothesis omega <= 1/2 is not removable

on the float canonical operator (K = 2..5, L = 0.5..6 step 0.5) the resolvent derivative H(D^-1 (B - a)^-2 g) matches the product formula at all 22 resolved even roots below the odd floor (relative residual < 1e-8), a central difference agrees (< 2e-5), the sign rule holds at every root and 1 - T equals the eigenvalue-product ratio to 4e-15. At most one even root lies below the odd floor on this grid, so only the first (+) slope is exercised numerically.

C1: perturbing B_L off the rank-one relation breaks the product formula (relative residual up to 4.6e8); C2: the decreasing-order sign rule (-1)^{#{i : a_i > a_j}} fails at 7 roots, so the increasing count is the right convention

exact SymPy third Taylor coefficient of s = a - b* H^-1 b equals the general, symmetric and response forms on 18 seeded families: real symmetric of complement dimension 1..4 (dimension 1 is the 2x2 Schur toy model) and complex Hermitian of dimension 1..2 with the real-part form

C1: coefficient 3 instead of 6 on <b', R H' R b'> fails on all 18 families; C2: b(t0) != 0 breaks the formula on all 12 real families; C3: with s = s' = s'' = 0 at t0, s''' = 1 gives s > 0 and s''' = -1 gives s < 0 just to the right, matching the necessary sign

at 30 digits the direct pole/arch/prime value A_L[h] equals int R(e^t) h' + int (e^{-t/2} - rho) h on 50 cases (relative residual < 1e-28): complex polynomial tests t(L - t)p(t) and the contact form t^2 e(1 - t/L) with the Lean derivative, at ten apertures including L < log 2, the seam log 2 and points just past log 4 and log 7

C1: h(L) != 0 misses by exactly R(e^L) h(L); C2: dropping the main term 2 sqrt x misses by exactly -int e^{t/2} h; C3: dropping the chain-rule factor -1/L in the contact derivative gives a nonzero miss

Arb (256-bit) certifies -Re e_u(omega) - (pi^6/90) |M_3|^2 omega^7 > 0 at 232 cells: 29 Gaussian-integer legal odd vectors (K = 2..8, including the K = 2 generator) at eight rational apertures up to the B-angle, the aperture hypothesis itself certified; minimum ratio 1.996. At 40 digits the sine Taylor bound, the remainder bound |T_u + M_3 t^3/6| <= B |t|^5/120, the beta integral a^7/140 and B <= A_K ||u|| hold; the ratio tends to 16/7 as omega -> 0, so pi^6/90 is sharp up to the 7/16 product factor

C1: the constant (16/7)(1 + 1e-3) pi^6/90 fails at omega = 1e-4; C2: without the aperture restriction the K = 2 generator has e(1) = 20 > 0 (certified); C3: dropping oddness (adding an even part with M_2 = 4, keeping M_1 = 0 and M_3 = 12) makes Re e > 0 at small omega; C4: with M_3 = 0 (K = 3 fifth-moment witness) -e/omega^7 -> 0, so no positive omega^7 bound exists without m > 0
